questions.title: Why does the paper use fastText for math page retrieval instead of a transformer classifier?
questions.question_body: The authors train a fastText model on OpenWebMath positives and random Common Crawl negatives to recall math web pages. Why did they choose fastText (a linear bag-of-ngrams model) rather than a stronger transformer classifier? Are there trade-offs in recall/precision, speed, or robustness that motivated this choice?

questions.title: How exactly is the iterative data-collection loop structured and why are domains with >10% collected pages labeled "math-related"?
questions.question_body: The pipeline iteratively expands the seed corpus by marking domains as math-related when over 10% of that domain's pages were collected in iteration 1. Why was the 10% threshold chosen? Could this threshold bias toward small or specialized sites, and how does this choice affect precision and recall of math pages?

questions.title: How was near-deduplication performed on Common Crawl to get 40B HTML pages?
questions.question_body: The paper says URL-based deduplication and "near-deduplication" reduced Common Crawl to 40B pages. What algorithms or tools were used for near-deduplication (e.g., MinHash, simhash, Brotli fingerprints)? What similarity threshold and document unit (HTML, text blocks) were used?

questions.title: Why remove any 10-gram substring that matches an evaluation benchmark for decontamination?
questions.question_body: For decontamination they remove any text segment containing a 10-gram string that matches exactly with any benchmark substring (and handle shorter benchmarks with 3+ grams). Why pick 10-grams as the main filter granularity? How does this trade off between false negatives (missed contamination) and false positives (removing unrelated content)?

questions.title: How is the multilingual composition of the DeepSeekMath Corpus measured and controlled?
questions.question_body: The paper claims the corpus is multilingual (mainly English and Chinese) and that this benefits Chinese math benchmarks. How were languages identified (langid? heuristics)? What are the approximate proportions of English vs Chinese tokens, and were any special heuristics applied to ensure high-quality non-English math content?

questions.title: Why does code pre-training improve mathematical reasoning according to their experiments?
questions.question_body: They report that starting from a code-trained model (DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5) or doing code training before math training improves math reasoning. What are the hypothesized mechanisms (e.g., exposure to structured syntax, algorithmic patterns, symbolic manipulation) and which experiments isolate which mechanism?

questions.title: Why did adding arXiv tokens not improve mathematical reasoning in their experiments?
questions.question_body: The authors find arXiv-only training did not help and even sometimes hurt math benchmarks. What are the possible explanations? Could it be domain mismatch (formal LaTeX vs informal problem-solving), noise in arXiv processing, lack of worked examples, or model size limitations? What processing pipelines of arXiv did they try and how might that affect results?

questions.title: What is the precise definition of a "reasoning step" in the process supervision setup?
questions.question_body: Process supervision scores each reasoning step and uses indices index(j) for end token of step j. How are steps detected or defined (sentence boundaries, explicit '\n\n', 'Step 1', or via a step-splitting model)? Is step segmentation deterministic across outputs with different lengths?

questions.title: In outcome supervision, why set the per-token advantage \(\hat{A}_{i,t}\) equal to the normalized final reward \(\widetilde{r}_i\)?
questions.question_body: Outcome supervision assigns the same normalized final reward to every token in the output: \(\hat{A}_{i,t} = \widetilde{r}_i\). How does this influence credit assignment for long multi-step solutions, and does it risk washing out which intermediate tokens actually led to the final correct answer?

questions.title: How exactly is the group-relative advantage \(\hat{A}_{i,t}\) computed in GRPO for process supervision?
questions.question_body: The paper says for process supervision \(\hat{A}_{i,t} = \sum_{index(j) \ge t} \widetilde{r}_i^{index(j)}\). What is the order and normalization used for \(\widetilde{r}_i^{index(j)}\) (are they normalized per-group across all steps of all outputs?), and how are tokens before the first step handled?

questions.title: Why does GRPO avoid training a critic and how does using group averages act as a baseline?
questions.question_body: PPO uses a value function baseline to compute advantages; GRPO replaces this with the group's mean reward. Conceptually, how does subtracting the group's mean (and dividing by std) reduce variance compared to a learned critic? Are there scenarios where GRPO's baseline is biased or has higher variance?

questions.title: What is the rationale for sampling a large group size (e.g., \(G=64\)) per question in GRPO?
questions.question_body: They sample 64 outputs per question and normalize rewards across the group. Why choose 64? How does group size affect stability, variance of advantage estimates, compute cost, and the ability to estimate meaningful group statistics (mean/std)?

questions.title: Why normalize rewards by subtracting group mean and dividing by group standard deviation?
questions.question_body: GRPO normalizes rewards within each group as \(\widetilde{r}_i = (r_i - \mathrm{mean}(\mathbf{r}))/\mathrm{std}(\mathbf{r})\). Why use standard score normalization instead of, say, min-max or centering only? Could dividing by a small std lead to extreme scaled advantages?

questions.title: The KL estimator used: derivation and correctness of \(\mathbb{D}_{KL}[\pi_\theta || \pi_{ref}] = \frac{\pi_{ref}}{\pi_\theta} - \log\frac{\pi_{ref}}{\pi_\theta} - 1\)?
questions.question_body: The paper uses an "unbiased estimator" \(x - \log x - 1\) with \(x = \frac{\pi_{ref}}{\pi_\theta}\). How is this derived as an estimator of KL, and under what expectation does it equal the true KL? I thought the KL between distributions is \(\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta}[\log \frac{\pi_\theta}{\pi_{ref}}]\). Can you show the derivation and assumptions for this estimator?

questions.title: How is the KL regularizer implemented in practice in GRPO (per-token vs aggregated)?
questions.question_body: GRPO directly adds \(\beta \mathbb{D}_{KL}[\pi_\theta || \pi_{ref}]\) to the per-token loss. Is this computed per-token log-probabilities, and is the KL summed/averaged across tokens in an output? How does this differ from PPO's per-token KL penalty in Eq. (2)?

questions.title: Why set the reference model to the current policy every outer iteration in Algorithm 1?
questions.question_body: Algorithm 1 sets \(\pi_{ref} \leftarrow \pi_\theta\) at the start of each outer iteration. Why not keep the initial SFT model as reference (as often done in RLHF)? What stability or regularization properties does updating the reference confer?

questions.title: How is the reward model trained and what labels are used to teach it to score math solutions?
questions.question_body: They say they "construct the training set of reward models following \citep{wang2023math}". Does this mean they label outputs by correctness of final answer, stepwise correctness, or human preference? How many labeled pairs/triplets, and what annotator protocol was used?

questions.title: In the unified paradigm equation (Eq. 18), what are concrete forms of the gradient coefficient \(GC_{\mathcal{A}}\) for SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO?
questions.question_body: Equation \(\nabla_\theta \mathcal{J}_\mathcal{A} = \mathbb{E}_{(q,o)\sim\mathcal{D}} [ (1/|o|) \sum_t GC_\mathcal{A}(q,o,t,\pi_{rf}) \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(o_t|q,o_{<t}) ]\). Can you write out the explicit GC functions for SFT (maximum likelihood), RFT (filtering by correct answers), DPO, PPO, and GRPO to see their differences concretely?

questions.title: What is the computational/memory advantage of GRPO compared to PPO given no critic?
questions.question_body: The paper claims GRPO reduces training resources by not training a value function. But GRPO samples G outputs per question (e.g., 64) and needs reward model inference on all of them. Can you provide a rough comparison of memory and compute (policy model forward/backward, reward model cost, and critic cost) between PPO and GRPO for a typical batch size?

questions.title: Why does iterative GRPO retrain the reward model with a 10% replay buffer, and how does that replay work?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 1 they continually train the reward model using a replay mechanism that incorporates 10% historical data. How is that historical data stored and sampled? Is 10% of each mini-batch replaced with historical samples, and how sensitive are results to this 10% choice?

questions.title: How are decoding and sampling parameters (temperature, top-p) chosen for generating the G outputs used in GRPO?
questions.question_body: The effectiveness of group baselines and advantage estimates depends on the diversity of sampled outputs. Did the authors use nucleus sampling (top-p), temperature, or other decoding strategies to produce the G outputs? If so, what values and why?

questions.title: What are the definitions of Pass@K and Maj@K used to analyze RL effects?
questions.question_body: They say RL improves Maj@K but not Pass@K, suggesting RL shifts probability mass to correct outputs in TopK. What are the precise definitions of Pass@K and Maj@K as used here, and how were they computed from sampled outputs?

questions.title: Why does GRPO+Process Supervision outperform GRPO+Outcome Supervision in their experiments?
questions.question_body: The authors observe that process supervision (per-step rewards) is better than outcome-only supervision. Could this simply be because process supervision provides denser signals, or are there specifics about the math tasks and reward model training that make process supervision especially helpful?

questions.title: How sensitive are GRPO results to hyper-parameters like \(\varepsilon\), \(\beta\), learning rate, and KL coefficient?
questions.question_body: They mention values: policy LR 1e-6, KL coefficient 0.04, sample size 64, etc. How sensitive is final performance to these choices, and were any hyper-parameter sweeps done (especially for \(\beta\) and \(\varepsilon\))?

questions.title: How is the reward-model uncertainty handled or estimated during RL training?
questions.question_body: In Section 6.2 the authors mention as future work the need to reflect reward-model uncertainty. In the current work, does the reward model provide any confidence or calibration score used in GRPO, or is it a point estimate? If not, could uncertain reward predictions harm training?

questions.title: How is formal proof success measured when using Sledgehammer with model-generated sketches?
questions.question_body: For the formal theorem proving experiments, they generate proof sketches and run Sledgehammer to fill details. What is the success criterion (Isabelle accepts proof?), and how robust is the pipeline to variations in sketch style? How many timeouts or invalid proofs occur?

questions.title: Why does one-stage mixed training of code+math sometimes harm non-tool math reasoning?
questions.question_body: They report that mixing code and math tokens in one-stage training can hurt math reasoning without tools for small models, while two-stage (code then math) works better. What is the hypothesized capacity/memory interference mechanism here, and are there mitigation strategies (e.g., curriculum, loss weighting, adapters)?

questions.title: Does normalizing rewards across all steps \(\mathrm{mean}(\mathbf{R})\)/\(\mathrm{std}(\mathbf{R})\) in process supervision cause leakage across outputs?
questions.question_body: Process supervision normalizes step rewards by mean/std over the whole set \(\mathbf{R}\) (which includes steps from all outputs in the group). Could this cause reward scaling to depend on extreme step scores from a single output and thereby introduce instability or undesired coupling across outputs?
